summary: Kootenai County lookout: L-4 cab on a pole tower built 1934; cab moved to Twin Crags in 1946; FFLA lists the tower as gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a pole tower
facts.status_note: FFLA list shows the tower as gone; no source describes what remains on the site today

events.note: Pole tower with L-4 cab. Height 40 ft per firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts; 30 ft per Forest Lookouts.
L-4 cab moved to Twin Crags Lookout. WillhiteWeb says a 20-foot pole tower with L-4 cab was moved.
Cab sold to a farmer, per WillhiteWeb (the Twin Crags tower, not the Echo Peak site).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say 40-foot pole; Forest Lookouts says 30-foot pole. Facts use the two-source value; the story reports the disagreement.

firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and Forest Lookouts say the cab moved to Twin Crags in 1946. WillhiteWeb says a 20-foot pole tower with L-4 cab moved. The story says the cab moved and notes the whole-tower account.
FFLA list calls the Twin Crags tower ruins; WillhiteWeb says the tower was still there in 2025 with no cab. Both are reported; no later source found.

sources.title: Latour Peak and Twin Crags Lookout

notes_for_editor: No source describes the Echo Peak site today; story says so. Height is disputed (40 ft vs 30 ft); correction proposed to 12.2 m for editor review. Twin Crags status conflicts (FFLA ruins vs 2025 standing tower). Twin Crags has its own record that was not checked. NHLR page slug guessed at nhlr.org/lookouts/us/id/echo-peak-lookout returned 404. No photos added. Story kept to sourced facts only. Height is 12.2 m (40 ft, two-source value) in facts; the earlier corrections entry (current 9.1 m, proposed 12.2 m) was removed as already applied, and the editor should confirm the 12.2 m value. North Idaho was dropped from the story because no cited page says it. The Twin Crags same-county sentence now cites source 4.
